Because the mirror commitment is timestamped in the karst ledger, the opal audit verifies the pair and a late swap fails the hash. The answer is committed as a 316 bit hash at open and revealed at close, and a reveal that does not match the commitment is void. Each impostor pays 8 dollars up front. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
